gloss: to wake up; to come to one's senses

definitions.gloss: to wake up; to open one's eyes
definitions.explanation: To transition from sleep to wakefulness.

definitions.gloss: to come to one's senses; to snap out of it
definitions.explanation: To realize the truth of a situation or abandon an illusion or misguided course of action.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}6{時|じ}に{目|め}を{覚|さ}ました。
examples.english: I woke up at 6 in the morning.

examples.japanese: {物音|ものおと}で{目|め}を{覚|さ}ますことがある。
examples.english: I sometimes wake up from a noise.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}ちゃんが{夜中|よなか}に{何度|なんど}も{目|め}を{覚|さ}ますので{寝不足|ねぶそく}だ。
examples.english: The baby wakes up many times during the night, so I'm sleep-deprived.

examples.japanese: いいかげん{目|め}を{覚|さ}ませ。
{友人|ゆうじん}の{言葉|ことば}で{目|め}を{覚|さ}ました。
examples.english: My friend's words made me come to my senses.

examples.japanese: {失敗|しっぱい}を{経験|けいけん}してようやく{目|め}を{覚|さ}まし、{自分|じぶん}の{甘|あま}さに{気|き}づいた。
examples.english: After experiencing failure, I finally came to my senses and realized my own naiveté.

notes:
A common expression with both literal (waking up) and figurative (coming to one's senses) meanings. The verb {覚|さ}ます means "to awaken" (transitive), so {目|め}を{覚|さ}ます literally means "to awaken one's eyes."

COMMON PATTERNS:
- Intransitive use: {目|め}が{覚|さ}める — to wake up (spontaneous; eyes open on their own)
- Transitive use: {目|め}を{覚|さ}ます — to wake (oneself) up / to awaken someone
- Causative: {目|め}を{覚|さ}まさせる — to make someone wake up / come to their senses
- {朝|あさ}{早|はや}く{目|め}を{覚|さ}ます — to wake up early in the morning
- 〜で{目|め}を{覚|さ}ます — to wake up because of ~
- いいかげん{目|め}を{覚|さ}ませ — snap out of it already (imperative)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {起|お}きる — to get up (more general; includes getting out of bed)
- {目覚|めざ}める — to awaken (literary/formal equivalent)
- {我|われ}に{返|かえ}る — to come to oneself (figurative only; more dramatic)
